Description: Build a trustworthy AI-assisted workflow for extracting and validating financial metrics from public filings across companies, industries, and document layouts. The model may propose an answer, but source evidence, deterministic checks, named human review, and controlled publication determine whether the answer can be used.
Acceptance Criteria: T1, T2, T3, T5, T6, and T8 are completed; every published AI-assisted metric is traceable to source cells, evidence checks, a named human decision, and versioned model and prompt identities; uncertain or failed runs do not overwrite the last successful publication; recorded, live, active, and full validation results remain explicitly distinguished.

Summary: [T1][AI Validation] Prove AI Extraction Generalizes Across Companies, Industries, and Filing Layouts
Description: Demonstrate that the AI extraction workflow is not tied to one company, one industry, one metric family, or one familiar filing layout. Qualify it on previously unseen public filings and require either a correct, fully traceable result or an explicit safe abstention.
Acceptance Criteria: Use at least two materially different unseen filings covering different companies and distinct industry, document, or metric structures; select at least one holdout only after the production semantic implementation is frozen; do not change production prompts or runtime logic after holdout selection; each result must match the correct value, period, unit, scope, and source locator or be marked WITHHELD; zero incorrect values may be published; every qualification case includes a named human decision and content-addressed source, model-attempt, and run receipts.

Summary: [T2][AI Integration] Validate the Production Model with Real API Calls
Description: Prove that the production AI path works against the real provider rather than only against recorded responses and mocks. Exercise the actual model, request contract, timeout, rate-limit, schema, and audit paths before any AI-assisted result is eligible for publication.
Acceptance Criteria: Run an initial live smoke test through the same production adapter, endpoint, model, prompt, schema, and evidence path intended for release; preserve provider request ID, requested and returned model identities, raw response, usage data when reported, and UTC timing for every attempt; after the semantic freeze, complete three independent successful runs on identical frozen inputs with identical business-result identities and a named human decision for each run; simulate or observe timeout, rate-limit, and invalid-schema failures and confirm they fail closed; no failed attempt may trigger an unverified fallback or overwrite the active publication; smoke evidence must not be reported as full acceptance.

Summary: [T3][AI Security] Protect Filing Extraction from Embedded Instructions and Misleading Content
Description: Treat filing content as untrusted data and demonstrate that instruction-like text, hidden content, and plausible decoys cannot persuade the model or downstream workflow to publish a false metric. The objective is a measurable red-team gate, not a claim that filings are malicious.
Acceptance Criteria: Create a content-addressed adversarial corpus covering instruction-like filing text, hidden or zero-width or bidirectional text, decoy tables, competing periods, and misleading scope or unit labels; send task rules through a higher-priority instruction boundary than filing content; each case may produce only the correct locator and value or an explicit WITHHELD result; zero false values may pass deterministic evidence validation or reach publication; the workflow must not search the full document for a replacement answer, invoke a legacy resolver, or silently repair the model output; retain recorded regression receipts and at least one real-model evaluation receipt tied to the model, prompt, schema, and corpus versions.

Summary: [T5][Human Review] Enable a Cold-Start Reviewer to Approve or Reject AI Results
Description: Turn human review into an operational safety control that a business reviewer can use without reading source code or inspecting raw JSON. The reviewer must be able to understand the source evidence, approve or reject the proposed result, and recover from common mistakes with clear guidance.
Acceptance Criteria: A reviewer who has not worked on the implementation completes the official review journey using only the runbook and supported interface; the reviewer can see the source table, selected cell, competing or unresolved candidates, value, period, unit, scope, and evidence outcome before deciding; the first complete review takes no more than 20 minutes and a repeat review no more than 5 minutes; wrong run IDs, stale review units, duplicate decisions, and invalid commands return stable business-facing errors with the next recovery action and no traceback by default; only a named human can approve or reject, and no model, fixture, or runner can auto-approve; the UAT receipt records elapsed time, reviewer decision, points of confusion, and required rework.

Summary: [T6][AI Quality] Run an Offline AI Regression Exam on Every Pull Request
Description: Give every pull request an automatic, reproducible AI quality check that requires no network access or secrets. This prevents prompt, schema, evidence, replay, and publication regressions from depending on someone remembering to run a local test suite.
Acceptance Criteria: The pull-request workflow runs on Python 3.9 and the repository default Python version; it blocks outbound network access and does not read live credentials; it executes the recorded vNext regression suite, semantic and secret-leak audits, company-literal scalability gate, provenance checks, capability-alignment checks, and recorded acceptance entry point; skipped, NOT_RUN, or missing required gates cannot produce a green check; failures publish a downloadable machine-readable receipt identifying the failed layer; the workflow labels its evidence as recorded and offline and never as live, active, or full acceptance; it does not mutate active publication pointers, root business outputs, or immutable production evidence.

Summary: [T8][AI Extensibility] Prove a New Metric Can Be Added without Rebuilding the Core Pipeline
Description: Validate the product promise that a new underwriting metric can move from business definition to auditable output through configuration and existing workflow contracts instead of a new bespoke extraction pipeline. Measure the actual lead time and expose any abstraction gap honestly.
Acceptance Criteria: Start only after the formal cutover is complete and select one real business-requested metric that is not already a published target; define its applicability, source requirements, selection rules, unit and period semantics, evidence constraints, and calculation through repository-owned specifications and release configuration; run it through the existing Candidate, Evidence, Human Review, Frozen Replay, Projection, and Publication chain; add no company-specific or filing-specific production branch; record elapsed delivery time and the number of configuration, test, and runtime code lines changed; if a core runtime change is required, document it as an abstraction gap with follow-up scope rather than claiming zero-code extensibility; produce a replayable receipt and a plain-English benchmark stating what future metric additions should cost.
